stories.title: The Island
stories.fortuneLine: Feed the bird. The journal already knows you are not a harbor. You are a light that will not come in.
stories.body:
There was a woman who lived on an island with no harbor and one fire tower. She kept the fire for ships she rarely saw, and at night she watched the dark with a copper telescope, believing a sailor loved her.

His ship, far out, answered her lantern with flashes she read as a language: short, long, short — a grammar of devotion she had invented and then forgotten she invented.

She fed a bird on honey and tied pale ribbons to its legs, and sent it over the water with a letter. Trinkets came back in the tide: a button, a coin worn smooth, a splinter of painted wood. Never a letter.

One morning she found a sailor’s journal, swollen and salt-white, in the rocks beneath the tower. The last entry read: “Beacon present. Not responsive. Source unknown.”

She never sends the bird again. She still feeds it. At dusk she whispers to the empty water, “He sees me. He just doesn’t know it yet.”
